UPDATE: Fracking

By: Laura Byrne | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The debate about fracking is back on radars as government publishes new amended regulations for public comment.

Summary:
A decade ago, it was the source of a raging debate over the future of the Karoo. Fracking, or hydraulic fracturing, is a controversial mining method. Water, sand and chemicals are pumped into the ground at high pressure to open up cracks deep underground and release oil and gas. It’s illegal in several countries, including South Africa. But now that’s about to change. In 2012, government lifted a year-old moratorium, allowing companies to apply for exploration licences. There was immediate backlash from civil and environmental groups across the country. In 2019, a long court battle came to an end when the Supreme Court of Appeal declared the initial fracking regulations unlawful, ordering that responsibility for the environmental regulation lies with the Department of Environmental Affairs – not the Department of Mineral Resources. But now the fight is back on. The amended regulations have incorporated recommendations by TKAG and others, but Deal says there are still significant concerns, like the fact that companies aren’t required to assess the health of surrounding communities before exploration begins. When a well closes, toxic chemicals can leach into the ground and water – but if information about the chemicals used is no longer available, there is no way to assess or reduce the damage. And strangest of all: a clause that allows automatic approval of licences. The public has until the 7th of December to comment on the amended regulations. If they pass, it's estimated that full-scale fracking will begin in the Karoo – and perhaps elsewhere - within the next two to three years.
